name: Caatinga Cacholote
rangeDescription: Arid northeastern brazil (pernambuco, piauí, bahia, and minas gerais)
description: Unmistakable. Large ovenbird with uniform cinnamon plumage, bushy crest, and yellow eyes.

name: Saddle-billed Stork
rangeDescription: Locally in sub-saharan africa
description: A tall, lanky, black-and-white stork with a unique red, yellow, and black bill. The male has dark-brown eyes, and the female has yellow eyes.

name: Rüppell's Warbler
rangeDescription: Rocky slopes of eastern mediterranean region; winters in northeastern africa
description: Fairly large Curruca warbler. Male is distinctive with a black bib and blackish head separated by prominent white moustache.

name: Banggai Fruit-Dove
rangeDescription: Peleng and banggai, in banggai islands (off eastern sulawesi)
description: A large gray-and-green fruit-dove confined to the Banggai Islands. Upperparts are forest-green and head and underparts are very pale gray, except for the wine-red vent, the tiny maroon chin, and the maroon base to the yellow bill.

name: Semiplumbeous Hawk
rangeDescription: Humid forest of honduras to western colombia and northwestern ecuador
description: Small forest hawk, usually seen perched inconspicuously in the canopy or at the forest edge. White below and gray above with distinctive orange-red legs and bill.

name: Black-faced Cotinga
rangeDescription: Tropical southeastern peru (southern ucayali and southern madre de dios)
description: A distinctively plumaged, vocal cotinga. Light gray, with darker gray wings and a black face.

name: Ring-billed Gull
rangeDescription: North america; winters to southern mexico, bahamas, and greater antilles
description: Fairly small gull, common and widespread throughout most of North America. Breeding adults are white-headed with a bold black ring around the bill; nonbreeding adults have smudgy brown markings on the head.

name: Eastern Bearded-Greenbul
rangeDescription: Cameroon to eastern democratic republic of the congo, northern angola, and far western uganda
description: A large greenbul often found in family groups or flocks in forest and forest edge with other bearded-greenbuls. Like all bearded-greenbuls, will sometimes puff out throat feathers.

name: Buff-breasted Tody-Tyrant
rangeDescription: Lowlands of eastern brazil (ceará, pernambuco, and alagoas)
description: Unobtrusive, drab little brownish flycatcher. Olive-backed, pale below, with the head looking disproportionately large compared to the rest of the body.

name: Pectoral Sandpiper
rangeDescription: Breeds arctic north america and siberia; winters to southern south america, australia
description: Beefy, medium-sized sandpiper. Brown-toned overall with yellowish legs.

name: Biak Hooded Pitta
rangeDescription: Biak (cenderawasih bay, off northwestern new guinea)
description: Beautiful leaf-green pitta of Biak Island, off northwestern New Guinea. Like the other “Hooded-type” pittas with which it was formerly grouped, this species has a black head, powder-blue shoulder patch, and red on the lower belly and undertail.

name: Ferruginous Duck
rangeDescription: Discontinuous palearctic; winters to india, southeastern asia, and eastern china
description: Rich rusty brown overall with contrasting white triangular patch under tail; male has pale eye. Also note peaked crown and rather long gray bill.

name: Sind Woodpecker
rangeDescription: Arid woodland and desert scrub of southeastern iran to pakistan
description: Only black-and-white woodpecker in most of its range. Note the big white shoulder patches and white bars on the black back.

name: Hammond's Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Breeds western north america; winters to nicaragua
description: Small grayish flycatcher, very similar to other flycatchers, especially Dusky and Gray. Subtle differences include smaller bill with limited pale base, slightly more peaked crown, and longer wingtips.

name: Blue-headed Racquet-tail
rangeDescription: Southern philippines (balabac, palawan, calamian, and adjacent islands)
description: A medium-sized parrot of lowland forest and edge on Palawan and neighboring islands. The two central tail feathers have extended shafts ending in a racket shape.

name: Amazonian Elaenia
rangeDescription: Eastern colombia to eastern ecuador, northeastern peru, southern venezuela, and northwestern brazil
description: Small flycatcher of rainforest canopy. Gray male is fairly distinctive with his black wings and bold, white wingbars.

name: Mamberamo Sunbird
rangeDescription: Northwestern new guinea and sepik ramu
description: Tiny and active sunbird of northern New Guinea. Male is dark gray-brown above, with an iridescent blue-black throat and black belly; small orange shoulder “spur” sometimes visible.

name: Chestnut-backed Laughingthrush
rangeDescription: Lowlands of northeastern india (arunachal pradesh) to northern myanmar
description: A myna-sized bird with a large white cheek patch and a black forehead, chin, and throat. Note the gray belly, the reddish back, and a small white patch on the forehead.

name: South Island Oystercatcher
rangeDescription: Highlands of south island (new zealand); winters to north island
description: Heavy-set black-and-white shorebird, affectionately known by New Zealand birders as “SIPO” (rhymes with “typo”). Shows a distinctive red eye, long thick reddish bill, and thick pale-pink feet and legs.

name: Large Lifou White-eye
rangeDescription: Forest of lifou island (loyalty islands)
description: A bizarre, large and heavy-billed white-eye that is notably distinctive among a group of birds famed for being homogeneous. Note gray plumage overall contrasting with olive head and wings.
